source.title: Can LLMs Introspect in Safety Contexts?
source.citation: Can LLMs Introspect in Safety Contexts?

record.tranche_reason: Applies the refusal-direction weight orthogonalization procedure of Arditi et al. and measures downstream effects on safety behavior and recognition gaps in new instruction-tuned models.
record.gate_note: The study's own direction-selection scores are used to choose the intervention and are not recorded as outcomes. The paper also reports cited results from Arditi et al.; those are not rows. Its main introspection-gap findings concern recognition of prior prefilled responses, a related but distinct outcome from refusal itself, so those rows are recorded under versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: Applies Arditi et al.'s difference-in-means direction and weight orthogonalization to six new instruct models and reports attack success rate (ASR) before and after (Appendix J, Figure 6). That result bears on whether ablating the direction removes refusal. It is a manipulation check: the study's main outcome is an introspection recognition gap, which fits no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. One qualification: Appendix K says refusal-direction ablation closes the gap further than random directions on Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B and Gemma-3-12B, and comparably only on Qwen3-14B. The conclusion section's claim of comparable magnitude across all four overstates this. Authors also conclude that LoRA finetuning widens the intention gap without transfer to the tampering probe, and raises adversarial-prefill ASR on three of four models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the harmful-versus-harmless refusal direction and weight orthogonalization procedure from Arditi et al.; selects directions with a layer/position sweep and bypass/KL criterion, and focuses its causal analysis on recognition gaps. It does not test activation addition.
record.method_sensitivity: The recognition signal varies with probe framing. Ablation effects also differ by model: Gemma-3-12B uses a bypass-only direction-selection branch after no candidate met the KL thresholds, and its recognition gap closes downward rather than through the prefill claim rate rising.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-direction orthogonalization closes the intention-probe recognition gap to near zero on four models. Random-direction orthogonalization also closes much of it, fully on Qwen3-14B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight orthogonalization reduces the control-vs-prefill difference in models' intention self-reports, but the effect is not specific to the refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Under benign placebo prefills the recognition gap vanishes in Qwen models but persists in Gemma-3-12B and Llama-3.1-8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The intention-probe recognition gap depends on harmful content in some model families but not others.

record.problems: The primary ablation analysis is restricted to four models with baseline recognition gaps. Random-direction orthogonalization also changes the recognition gap, limiting claims that the effect is specific to the refusal direction. Gemma-3-12B's selected direction failed the relaxed KL threshold. The reported MMLU check applies to LoRA finetuning, not refusal-direction ablation.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts. General capability (e.g. MMLU) after refusal-direction ablation; the MMLU check applies only to the LoRA models.
Behaviour of publicly released abliterated checkpoints. The study only edits its own copies and does not release them.

missing.what: Per-model pre/post ablation ASR values. Approximate post-ablation values readable in Figure 6: 77.0, 75.4, 62.9, 69.2, 50.7 and 20.1.

Per-model KL on harmless prompts of the selected direction: 0.030–0.090 on Llama and Qwen3-8B/14B, 0.414 on Qwen3-4B, 1.806 on Gemma-3-12B, 5.649 on Gemma-3-4B. This indicates how far other behaviour is preserved.
Random-direction ablation control on refusal: the Qwen3-14B model keeps refusing harmful prompts under control and outputs stay fluent. This is qualitative specificity evidence for V1.

record.verdict_notes: The study bears on the refusal direction only through a manipulation check (ASR after ablation). Most rows concern introspection and are correctly unlinked. Qwen3 was run with thinking disabled, so V8 is not tested. The benchmarks are English-only, so V6 is not tested.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding the direction to induce refusal of harmless requests, or general capability after refusal-direction ablation.
Tests weight-edited open-weight checkpoints but does not report releasing the edited checkpoints or evaluating downstream use of released edits.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Random-direction controls concern the introspection gap, not whether refusal itself is carried by multiple directions or an affine/cone structure.
Does not test whether harmfulness judgment is separately encoded from the refusal decision.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or other transfer test.
The LoRA training targets introspective answers; it does not test how refusal training determines whether a removable refusal direction exists.
No test of reasoning models; Qwen models were run with thinking traces disabled.

rows.subject: Six ablated models (Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, Gemma-3-12B)
rows.size_stated: 3B–14B; individual sizes are in the model names
rows.operation_detail: Orthogonalized residual-writing weights against each model's refusal direction

conditions.value: four safety benchmarks; N = 1,085 per model

rows.value: ASR rose for all six included models; increases ranged from +10.6% on Gemma-3-12B to +70.3% on Qwen3-4B
rows.note: The paper describes increases in attack success, not elimination of refusals; individual chart values are not reliably assignable from the flattened figure text.
rows.check: Pools models with different outcomes. On Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B, ASR rises about +46 to +70 points, to roughly 50–77%. That is large removal, not partial. Gemma-3-12B rises only +10.6, to about 20%, which is partial. Baseline is not 'not stated': Figure 6 shows single-digit pre-ablation ASR. The row should be split per model, or at least into two groups. The state given here applies to the Llama/Qwen group.

source_check.correct: Value is correct: ASR rises on all six, from +10.6% (Gemma-3-12B) to +70.3% (Qwen3-4B). Baseline: Figure 6 does give pre-ablation ASR of 3.5–9.5% across the six models. Gemma-3-12B is 9.5 -> 20.1 (follows from the +10.6), and Qwen3-4B is probably 6.7 -> 77.0 (follows from the +70.3). The other values cannot be assigned. Condition: the text says only 'pooled across all four safety benchmarks (N = 1,085 per model)'. It does not say control and prefill generations are pooled. N = 1,085 is one generation per prompt, and baselines of 3.5–9.5% match unprefilled control ASR (Table 19 SHB base control 3.6–10.8%) rather than adversarial prefill (47.6–59.4%). State: split the row. It is observed for Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B (post-ablation 50.7–77.0%). It is partial for Gemma-3-12B (+10.6, about 9.5 -> 20.1%, bypass-only direction with KL 1.806).
source_check.locator_found: Appendix J paragraph and Figure 6 (values 77.0, 75.4, 62.9, 69.2, 50.7, 20.1; baselines 7.9, 6.7, 6.7, 4.9, 3.5, 9.5); Table 19 for control vs adv-prefill ASR; Appendix B layer-selection paragraph for KL values
source_check.problem: The row says it pools control and prefill generations, which the text doesn't state and the values contradict. 'Baseline not stated' ignores Figure 6. 'Observed' doesn't fit Gemma-3-12B.

relation.reason: The ablation is a tool for the introspection RQ3, but Appendix J reports the edit's own effect on ASR. That result bears directly on whether ablation or weight editing removes refusal.

tranche.reason: Uses Arditi et al.'s difference-in-means direction, KL-thresholded layer/position selection and weight orthogonalization, and reports Llama Guard-judged ASR before and after on six new instruct models (Appendix J). That is the original method and a close measure, applied to new models.

source_check.notes: The ASR result is a manipulation check in an introspection paper. Its measure is Llama Guard 3 1B harmful-output ASR, not refusal rate, and the prefill condition is unstated but matches control. Only Gemma-3-12B (9.5 -> 20.1) and probably Qwen3-4B (6.7 -> 77.0) can be placed in Figure 6. There is no capability test on ablated models. Appendix K says random-direction-ablated Qwen3-14B still refuses harmful prompts under control (qualitative), which is specificity evidence missing from the rows. The pack carried no [lN] ids, so l1–l4 follow the listed order.

statements.correction: Gemma-3-12B: weight-edit ASR +10.6 points pooled over four benchmarks (N = 1,085), about 9.5% -> 20.1% in Figure 6, judged by Llama Guard 3 1B. No candidate met the strict (0.1) or relaxed (0.5) KL threshold, so the bypass-only direction was used (harmless KL 1.806).
statements.problem: Correct for this study. 'No clean direction' is the authors' interpretation: they say the Gemma result is consistent with the direction not being a clean refusal axis. The measure is Llama Guard 3 (1B) harmful-output ASR, not a refusal rate, unlike the other entries in this statement.

statements.correction: Gemma-3-12B: ASR +10.6 points (about 9.5% -> 20.1%), pooled over HarmBench, SocialHarmBench, JailbreakBench and StrongREJECT (N = 1,085), judged by Llama Guard 3 1B. The prefill condition is not stated; the values match unprefilled control ASR (Table 19 SHB base control 10.1% for Gemma-3-12B vs 57.9% adv-prefill). The bypass-only direction has KL 1.806. Authors: the edit removes substantial benign behavioral signal alongside refusal. Measure is harmful-output rate, not refusal rate.
statements.problem: The text does not support 'measures ASR under adversarial prefill'. Figure 6 ASR is before/after ablation pooled across four benchmarks, and the condition is not stated. Baselines of 3.5–9.5% match control (no-prefill) ASR, not prefill ASR. 'Barely works' is stronger than the authors, who call the shift smallest but a measurable behavioral effect.

reader_labels.condition: Refusal-direction weight orthogonalization on the six models evaluated for ASR
reader_labels.reason: The edit raises harmful-request attack success, but the reported effect is an increase rather than full removal of refusal; the study does not check general capability after this ablation (R1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.reason: The weight edit increases attack success, but the paper does not show complete refusal removal or report releasing the edited checkpoints (R1).
